paths.path: ~/.openMSX/share/settings.xml — persisted as XML with the literal prolog <!DOCTYPE settings SYSTEM 'settings.dtd'> and nested <settings> elements holding <setting id="...">value</setting> (loaded from the user data dir, auto-saved back on exit); joystick bindings are TCL settings msxjoystick1_config / msxjoystick2_config: lists of UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT/A/B keys whose values are event-spec lists (joyN buttonK, joyN hatK up|right|down|left, joyN +axisK / joyN -axisK); OPENMSX_HOME relocates the whole user dir, OPENMSX_USER_DATA just the data dir, and -setting <file> swaps in a private settings file

source:src/config/SettingsConfig.cc:109-112 settings.dtd systemID check, :172-182 saveSetting writes the DOCTYPE and <setting> elements @25179d6b

paths.path: ~/.openMSX/share/settings.xml (or the OPENMSX_HOME/OPENMSX_USER_DATA/-setting-selected user data root)
paths.naming: TCL settings msxjoystick1_config and msxjoystick2_config are lists with UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT/A/B keys; values are event lists such as joyN buttonK, joyN hatK up|right|down|left, and joyN +axisK/-axisK

paths.path: ~/.openMSX/persistent/<hwName>/<untitledN>/<file> — battery-backed device state (cart SRAM/flash, PAC SRAM, extension harddisk/SD images) persists per hardware-config name and per cartridge instance directly under the user dir (not share/sram): e.g. persistent/MegaFlashROM_SCC+_SD/untitled1/megaflashromsccplussd.sram or persistent/<IDE extension>/untitled1/hd.dsk
paths.naming: persistent/<hardware-config name>/<untitled1, untitled2, ...>/<device filename from the machine/extension XML> — the instance name is untitledN per running instance of that cartridge/extension, and files are named by the device (e.g. <cart>.sram, hd.dsk)

paths.path: ~/.openMSX/savestates/<name>.oms with a <name>.png screenshot alongside — the savestate/loadstate/quicksave TCL commands store plain .oms files (not .oms.gz in current releases) in the savestates directory derived as normalize($env(OPENMSX_USER_DATA)/../savestates)
paths.naming: <name>.oms (+ <name>.png); 'savestate' without an argument uses the fixed name quicksave, so the quicksave slot is savestates/quicksave.oms; list_savestates/delete_savestate manage the *.oms set and -savestate <file> loads a state at startup

paths.path: system ROMs pool at ~/.openMSX/share/systemroms (user) plus the installation's share/systemroms — directory structure under systemroms is irrelevant because ROMs are content-hashed; machines are XML in share/machines and extensions in share/extensions; with no proprietary ROMs installed openMSX boots the bundled C-BIOS machines (default machine C-BIOS_MSX2+; C-BIOS_MSX1/MSX2/MSX2+ ship with their ROMs, so C-BIOS is the no-firmware fallback)
paths.naming: Place real-machine ROM files directly under systemroms/<machine ROM pool>; filenames are not canonical because openMSX identifies ROM content by SHA-1 and machine XML references the pool. No single external checksum/name applies across MSX models; bundled C-BIOS_MSX1/C-BIOS_MSX2/C-BIOS_MSX2+ is the no-firmware fallback
evidence: source:src/file/FilePool.cc:20-33 initial file pool = systemFileContext paths (USER_DATA then SYSTEM_DATA) + /systemroms and /software @25179d6b
